clue.text: Wraps almost conceal David's work

indicators.note: the words wraps almost conceal the answer, which runs across their join

explanation.surface: An instruction to keep something nearly wrapped up and hidden, as if covering a piece of David's handiwork.
explanation.definitionFit: King David is traditionally credited as the author of the biblical psalms, the sacred songs he composed.

clue.text: The result of 24 trimmed sheets of paper

parts.note: a garment piped with braid is trimmed along its edges
a ream is a pack of about 500 sheets of paper

explanation.surface: A drug's after-effect, compared to some cut-down stationery.
explanation.walkthrough: 24 is OPIUM; an opium smoker's pipe brings fantasies, the origin of the phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: A fanciful, unrealisable hope was originally a vision induced by smoking an opium pipe.

clue.text: Revile Lincoln outside America

indicators.note: the name for Lincoln goes outside the abbreviation for America, enclosing it

parts.note: Abe is short for Abraham, as in Abraham Lincoln
US is the United States of America

explanation.surface: Someone insults President Lincoln when he is abroad.
explanation.definitionFit: To revile is to attack someone with insulting language.

clue.text: Bill and I see conserve put up in pots

indicators.note: in a down clue put up means the whole run of pieces is read from bottom to top

parts.note: ac is an abbreviation for account, a bill
lo is an archaic exclamation meaning look or see
jam is a fruit conserve

explanation.surface: Bill and I are bottling preserves in jars.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put up' turns the run AC + I + LO + JAM upwards, so it reads MAJ OL I CA.
explanation.definitionFit: Majolica is a tin-glazed Italian earthenware, used for decorated vessels and dishes.

clue.text: Keeping watch on anybody around the cargo space

indicators.note: the word for anybody is placed around the cargo space word, enclosing it

parts.note: a being is any creature or person
a ship's hold is where its cargo is stored

explanation.surface: Someone keeps a lookout on anyone loitering near a ship's hold.
explanation.definitionFit: To behold is an old word for to look at or observe, so watching something is beholding it.

clue.text: Musicians forbidden to talk

indicators.note: to talk means said out loud, so the word for forbidden is pronounced

parts.note: something forbidden is banned

explanation.surface: Players who have been forbidden from speaking.
explanation.definitionFit: A group of musicians playing together, such as a brass or rock group.

clue.text: He and I in a position to show indecision

indicators.note: in places I inside the word for a position

parts.note: a station is a post or position someone is assigned to

explanation.surface: A man and I are in a spot where we cannot make up our minds.
explanation.definitionFit: Hesitation is wavering through doubt, being unable to decide.

clue.text: All the characters in play capable of murder

indicators.note: the letters of all the are put into play, moving to new positions

explanation.surface: Every role in a drama belongs to someone who could kill.
explanation.definitionFit: Something deadly is able to kill, as a lethal weapon is.

clue.text: Batting, players dismissed for facing the wrong way

parts.note: in cricket a side that is batting is in
a side is a team of players
a batsman who is dismissed is out

explanation.surface: Cricket chatter: batting, with team members getting out.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, the batting side is said to be in, and a dismissed batsman is out.
explanation.definitionFit: A garment turned so that its lining shows is reversed, the wrong way round.

clue.text: Climbing, for instance, to see unusual birds

indicators.note: in a down clue climbing means read upwards, so the abbreviation is turned

parts.note: eg is the abbreviation for for example

indicators.note: unusual means the letters of see are put in a strange order

explanation.surface: Climbing, for example, to spot some rare birds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Climbing' turns EG into GE; 'unusual' rearranges SEE as ESE.
explanation.definitionFit: Ganders and their mates are large waterfowl kept on farms.

clue.text: American sailor's dance

explanation.surface: A US seaman's favourite jig.
explanation.definitionFit: John Paul Jones was a naval hero of the American Revolution, and a Paul Jones is also a ballroom mixer dance where partners change.

clue.text: Try to set a test

indicators.note: to set letters is to arrange them, so a test is put into a new order

explanation.surface: An examiner's job: to devise an exam.
explanation.definitionFit: To try food is to sample it, as in having a taste of a dish.

clue.text: The river to run unfathomably

parts.note: the Dee is a river in Scotland and also one on the England-Wales border
a ferry plies, or runs regularly, between two ports

explanation.surface: A river flowing on through bottomless depths.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unfathomable is too deep to sound, so it goes down to great depth.

clue.text: Back in days of yore, missiles put each side of target

indicators.note: back tells us the run of days of yore and missiles is read from right to left

parts.note: eld is an archaic word for old times
darts are small thrown missiles

explanation.surface: Long ago, missiles were set up around a target.
explanation.walkthrough: Back turns the whole run ELD + DARTS, giving STRAD + DLE. In gunnery, shots that straddle a target land on either side of it, finding the range.
explanation.definitionFit: Artillery fire that lands on both near and far sides of a target is said to bracket or span it.

clue.text: Where to find a koala in difficulties?

explanation.surface: Asking where to look for an Australian marsupial in trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: Koalas live among Australian eucalyptus trees, and the idiom for being stuck in a fix uses that same perch.

clue.text: Meat pie can get cooked free

indicators.note: to cook figures is to falsify them, so these letters are worked into another arrangement

explanation.surface: A kitchen note: the canned meat pie can be heated without charge.
explanation.definitionFit: To set slaves or a people at liberty is to release them, as in the Emancipation Proclamation.

clue.text: A very quiet part of London, but attractive

parts.note: pp is pianissimo, the musical marking for very quiet
Ealing is a district of west London

explanation.surface: A peaceful London suburb that is nevertheless appealing.
explanation.walkthrough: Ealing is a borough in west London, famous for its film studios.
explanation.definitionFit: Something attractive draws people in and charms them.

clue.text: What beaters do about game

indicators.note: about here means turned round, so the beaters' action is read backwards

parts.note: people who beat others flog them

explanation.surface: On a shoot, the beaters drive birds for the game.
explanation.walkthrough: On a shoot, beaters drive birds towards the guns, which the surface plays on; here they simply thrash, or flog.
explanation.definitionFit: Golf is a sport played with clubs on a course of eighteen holes.

clue.text: Boxer starts off letting you win easily in bout

indicators.note: in puts those initials inside the word for a bout

parts.note: a bout is a fight or contest

indicators.note: starts off means the opening letter of each of the four words letting, you, win, easily

explanation.surface: A boxer begins by letting his opponent win comfortably in the contest.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface pictures a boxer throwing a fight; in fact 'Boxer' is the definition, and 'easily' is the fourth initial, not an adverb.
explanation.definitionFit: A boxer in the lightest weight division, up to about 51 kg, competes as one of these.

clue.text: With 10 flutes at their disposal

indicators.note: disposal means arrangement, so the letters of flutes at are disposed in new order

explanation.surface: Musicians who have ten flutes available to them.
explanation.walkthrough: 10 is TASTE, so With 10 means having taste.
explanation.definitionFit: Showing good aesthetic judgement is having refined discernment.

clue.text: Moon, its first quarter poetically exposed to view

parts.note: its points back to Moon, and the first quarter of its four letters is M
ope is a poetic form of open, meaning uncovered or visible

explanation.surface: Poetic description of the moon in its first quarter coming into view.
explanation.definitionFit: To moon about is to wander listlessly, which is what someone who sulks dejectedly does.

clue.text: Unaware of any girl not having been made up

indicators.note: something made up is invented or composed, so these letters are reassembled

explanation.surface: Someone is oblivious to any girl who has not put on her make-up.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting without knowledge or awareness of something is doing it in an uninformed way.

clue.text: Henry falls from top to bottom of bluff — how like Henry!

indicators.text: falls from top to bottom of
indicators.note: in a down clue the letter falls from the top of the word for bluff to its foot

parts.note: a bluff is a cliff, a height
H is the symbol of the henry, the unit of inductance

explanation.surface: Henry topples off a clifftop to the base, much like a famous king.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition points to Henry VIII, whose regnal number is ordinal.
explanation.definitionFit: England's King Henry the Eighth bore this ordinal, so it is a fair way of describing him.

clue.text: Daily one's. mother exhibits a divine quality

parts.note: a daily is a British cleaning lady, also called a char or charwoman
one is I, and 's is is, giving I'S
ma is an informal word for mother

explanation.surface: A cleaning woman's mother shows a saintly aura.
explanation.walkthrough: A daily or char is a British term for a woman who comes in to clean houses.
explanation.definitionFit: In theology charisma is a gift of grace from God, and more widely a compelling personal magnetism.

clue.text: Go up country, we hear

indicators.note: we hear means the word for country sounds like the answer when spoken

parts.note: a clime is a region or country, especially in terms of its climate

explanation.surface: Heading up-country, according to report.
explanation.definitionFit: To ascend is to mount or scale a slope.

clue.text: Gently rub one in eight

explanation.surface: Caress one member of a rowing crew.
explanation.definitionFit: To caress is to pass a hand lightly over something; and in a rowing eight the oarsman setting the pace sits at the stern seat by that name.

clue.text: Drug enshrined in the hearts of 19. 26 and 13

indicators.note: the hearts of means the central letters of each of the three answers named

parts.note: refers to the answer at 19 across
refers to the answer at 26 across
refers to the answer at 13 down

explanation.surface: A narcotic hidden at the core of three other answers.
explanation.walkthrough: The centres are OP from MOPE, I from IRISH and UM from UP A GUM TREE.
explanation.definitionFit: A narcotic made from poppy sap, the source of morphine and heroin.

clue.text: Jack, the foreign expert

parts.note: a jack or jack tar is a sailor
le is French for the

explanation.surface: A sailor from overseas who is a specialist.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone skilled or competent at a task is capable.

clue.text: National flower first adopted by Hungary

indicators.note: the flower comes first and is then taken on by Hungary, which follows it

parts.note: the iris is a garden flower
H is the international vehicle code for Hungary

explanation.surface: Hungary takes on some country's national flower as its own.
explanation.definitionFit: Of a nationality: belonging to Ireland, its people or language.

clue.text: Being dismissive about cleaning method

parts.note: re means concerning or about
buffing is polishing a surface with a soft cloth

explanation.surface: Someone sniffy about the way the cleaning is done.
explanation.definitionFit: To snub or rebuff someone is to brush off their approach curtly.

clue.text: V.I.P. returns rock to Wensleydale, perhaps

indicators.note: returns means the word for rock is turned back to front

parts.note: Gib is a nickname for the Rock of Gibraltar
Wensleydale is a crumbly cheese from Yorkshire

explanation.surface: A dignitary goes back to a rocky part of the Yorkshire Dales.
explanation.walkthrough: Wensleydale is a valley in Yorkshire, England, and the crumbly cheese made there. The leading 3 in the held clue is not on the printed page.
explanation.definitionFit: An important person is informally called a big shot or big wheel.

clue.text: Check road with lights on both sides of it

indicators.note: the lights word sits on both sides of the road, which it refers to

parts.note: lit means illuminated, lit up by lights
the M1 is Britain's main motorway north from London, written MI

explanation.surface: A traffic control: a road with street lamps along both edges.
explanation.walkthrough: The M1 is Britain's first motorway, from London to Leeds; crosswords write it as MI.
explanation.definitionFit: To check something is to restrain or curb it, putting a cap on it.
